summary: Social impact was the week's heaviest category: 38 of 82 stories (46%) carried a negative social reading, against only 8 (10%) positive. Political coverage was also skewed, at 35% negative to 11% positive. Economic readings stayed mostly neutral (70%), with negatives (16%) only narrowly outnumbering positives (15%). The social and political pattern traces to two storylines that ran almost the whole week: the build up to PTI's planned September 27 march on Islamabad, and a sharp rise in violence and cross-border action in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and along the Afghan frontier.

The march dominated the flagged stories. Across the week, Miqyas tracked a sequence of official measures and opposition responses: the 30 day detention of Imran Khan's sister Aleema Khan under public order law, followed by the detention of two more sisters (which the Lahore High Court declined to suspend immediately), a reported deployment of more than 22,000 security personnel, Section 144 orders in Islamabad, Punjab and Balochistan, Rangers authorised in the capital and five Punjab districts, and a reported request to suspend mobile and internet service around Rawalpindi and Attock. The government said these steps were needed to stop violent groups reaching the capital and, per the finance minister, to avoid losses he put at roughly Rs120 billion a day; PTI called the detentions political victimisation and claimed around 1,500 arrests, and Amnesty International called the detentions a rights violation. Jamaat-e-Islami's separate long march against the petroleum levy added to the pressure on the capital. By Friday, Dawn reported PTI was still weighing its options, though its spokesperson said the march stands.

Security was the second thread. The week opened with a suicide blast and assault on Kohat Police Lines, with reported death tolls ranging from 17 to 31. Official accounts then described operations in Kohat and Hangu, strikes on militant targets across the Afghan border, eight drones shot down near Torkham and Kohat, and strikes on ten locations in Afghanistan that the information minister described as proportionate. Afghanistan's Taliban administration disputed at least one set of casualty figures. These stories rest heavily on official and security sources, which is why most were tagged with medium or low confidence. The economic picture was quieter and mixed: several fuel price adjustments (one petrol increase, then a run of cuts) and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's UNGA meetings, including with the IMF chief and EU officials, accounted for most positive economic readings, while negative ones mostly came from protest related disruption. Notably, September 23, the day UNGA diplomacy led the feed, was the only day with no flagged stories.

On lean, 78 of 82 stories (95%) were read as balanced, with 3 tagged pro-government and 1 pro-opposition, even though the week's coverage was about as politically charged as it gets. The few non-balanced tags fell on single source pieces carrying one side's statements, such as the interior minister's 'iron hands' warning and a PTI-sourced account of the sisters' arrests. Confidence was the weaker signal: only 23 stories (28%) were rated high, 50 medium and 9 low. The low confidence items clustered around unnamed-source claims, including a report linking India's RAW and the Taliban to attacks in Pakistan and an account of a foiled Taliban border incursion, and those should be read as unverified until corroborated.

notableStories.headline: At least 17 including cops martyred in Kohat blast
notableStories.context: A suicide blast and armed assault on Kohat Police Lines during Friday prayers opened a week of escalating violence in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with outlets reporting tolls between 17 and 31 dead.

notableStories.headline: Pakistan conducted strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan in response to recent drone attacks: info minister
notableStories.context: The information minister said Pakistan struck ten locations in Afghanistan after drones crossed into its airspace, a significant cross-border escalation resting so far on the government's own account.

notableStories.headline: Aleema Khan 'detained' in Lahore under 3MPO, 'shifted' to Kot Lakhpat jail
notableStories.context: The 30 day detention of Imran Khan's sister, which PTI called political revenge, started a run of detentions of Khan's relatives ahead of the September 27 march.

notableStories.headline: Roads blocked around capital ahead of planned PTI protest
notableStories.context: The clearest snapshot of the capital before the march: containers, around 22,000 security personnel, PTI's claim of about 1,500 arrests, Amnesty's criticism, and the information minister's denial of a lockdown.

notableStories.headline: JI kicks off long march towards Islamabad against petroleum levy
notableStories.context: Jamaat-e-Islami's march over the petroleum levy, after five failed rounds of talks, was the week's main economic protest and ran alongside PTI's plans.
